answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable identity bond. Each agent must lock its own collateral to earn one vote, and the shared ledger compounds reputation slowly, the way quartz forms under pressure; a cheating agent forfeits its bond as surely as opal shatters when struck. Since stake cannot be divided into costless copies, an attacker who wants a thousand votes must post a thousand separate deposits. Facing a flood of fake accounts as vast as a glacier, the up-front capital plus the constant risk of slashing make the attack far costlier than any gain.
